h: Abbeys, estates and a night on the lanes
p: The Light is right in the city centre, so getting there is easy on foot from Leeds station or by bus along the Headrow. Inside the complex you'll also find a cinema and places to eat, which makes it a handy one-stop spot for a full night out without having to walk across town in the rain.

A few practical bits. Bring photo ID if you look young, because bar-led venues commonly check. Book your lane ahead, especially at weekends, and if there are more than six of you, think about two lanes so nobody spends half the evening waiting. Agree teams and a forfeit before the first ball, and switch players halfway to keep it fair.

If you're in Leeds for a weekend, there are some brilliant places just outside the centre. Temple Newsam is a grand Tudor-Jacobean house set in vast parkland on the east side of the city, with a working farm that's a hit with families. Harewood House, a stately home with gardens, a bird garden and lakeside walks, sits a little further north. And Kirkstall Abbey, the ruins of a Cistercian monastery by the River Aire, makes a lovely photo spot.
Back in town, Leeds Playhouse puts on plays and touring shows, and Kirkgate Market is perfect for a cheap lunch. Combine a day out with an evening of bowling, and you've got a great weekend sorted.
